We achieve some of it by narrative design resonance. That is, cohesive narrative choices across all aspects of the game that feel specific, deliberate, and consistent, but it won't do all the work if your moments still end up not feeling specific enough to the experience the player is having.

Narrative specificity is challenging in games that have any sort of player agency, as it should be, but a lack of it is I think one of the things that make people categorize game writing as "not good." Resonance is tied to specificity, and resonance is what makes you feel something.
